His 2013 report also noted that Cole had pre-existing arthritic changes to his hips. Dr. Nadar noted Cole’s complaints of pain in his back and neck from his work injury (although he noted in 2017 that the neck claim had been dismissed) and that Cole denied suffering back or neck pain prior to his 2013 work injury. The ALJ could properly rely on Cole’s lay testimony concerning his experiencing symptoms and functional difficulties. See, e.g., Hush, supra. Sumitomo Electric Wiring, 481 S.W.3d 492, 496 (Ky. 2015) (citation omitted). But when the medical evidence on causation is uncontroverted, an ALJ may not properly rely on personal experience, inference, or lay testimony to disregard such uncontroverted medical proof. Id. Andrew Williams (Father) and Charlene M. Noel-Lang (Mother), unmarried parents of two children (ages 14 and 9), had prior agreements on custody and support for the older child, with Father paying $1,000 monthly. Father sought sole custody of the older child, while Mother moved to establish support and visitation for the younger child and enforce Father's obligation for the older. Father failed to provide income documentation despite court orders, leading the Kenton Circuit Court to impute his income at $150,000 annually as a CR 37 discovery sanction. The court awarded joint custody, set Father's visitation, ordered $1,613 monthly support for the younger child, found Father in contempt for $93,891.60 arrearage on the older child, and required purge by full payment within 180 days or 45 days incarceration (30 conditionally discharged). Father moved to reconsider, claiming inaccurate income imputation and inability to pay due to a tax lien, but provided no evidence. The circuit court denied the motion. On appeal, Father challenged the income imputation without shared parenting credit and the conditional jail sentence. The Court of Appeals affirmed, holding no abuse of discretion in the discovery sanction given Father's willful noncompliance, prejudice to Mother, warnings issued, and reasonableness tied to his self-employment and assets.
